cues.zh: 也就是一个普朗克常数单位。对于今晚而言，这基本上就是我们需要了解的全部量子力学知识了。下一个概念相对简单一些，至少我认为更简单，它是一个经典概念，也就是“场”的概念。场只是空间中的一种状态。它可以是电场，可以是磁场，也可以是引力场。无论你认为存在于空间中的是什么，

cues.en: Quantum mechanics, we're going to summarize by one simple statement that things are quantized in quantum mechanics. Quantized means they come in discrete bits. cues.en: Nothing happens. If you take one out, nothing happens. And let's ask now what that means. The left-handed electron coming in has a zilch of 1. Let's call it a Z of 1. The right-handed has Z equals 0. Back to the left-handed, Z equals 1. Is that possible? Only if you emit something at this point...
cues.zh: 什么都不会发生。如果你拿出来一个，也什么都不会发生。现在让我们问问这意味着什么。入射的左手电子具有为 1 的 zilch。我们称之为 Z 等于 1。右手电子的 Z 等于 0。再变回左手电子，Z 等于 1。这可能吗？除非你在此时发射出某种东西……

cues.en: which carries off that Z equals 1. A ziggs. The ziggs boson gets emitted. It carries a Z equals 1. But what happens to it? Where does it go? It goes into the condensate. It gets lost in the condensate. You put one in, and it just gets absorbed into the condensate. And so the electron goes on its merry way. The condensate absorbs
cues.zh: 带走那个 Z 等于 1。一个 ziggs。Ziggs 玻色子被发射出来了。它带有 Z 等于 1。但它会怎样呢？它去哪儿了？它进入了凝聚态。它消散在凝聚态中。你放进去一个，它就直接被凝聚态吸收了。于是电子继续愉快地前进。凝聚态吸收了

cues.en: the zilch, and it goes from 1 to 0, but then it can borrow a particle back from the condensate. Borrow one back, it doesn't even have to borrow it. If you pull one out, nothing changes again. And so it goes on its merry way from left-handed to right-handed, from left-handed to right-handed, every time it switches, it emits a particle carrying this zilch quantum number, which then just gets absorbed into the condensate.
cues.zh: zilch，它就从 1 变成了 0，但接着它又可以从凝聚态中借回一个粒子。借回一个，它甚至都不需要借。如果你抽出来一个，依然什么都没变。于是它就愉快地继续前进，从左手变成右手，从左手变成右手，每次切换，它都会发射一个带有这种 zilch 量子数的粒子，然后直接被凝聚态吸收。

cues.en: That's the mechanism by which a field, and in this case, it's a field which forms a condensate by itself. It doesn't require capacitor plates. It just requires the energy to be such that the field naturally gets shifted. And that's the mechanism by which electrons, quarks, and the various partners of those particles, the mu particle, the tau,
cues.zh: 这就是场的作用机制，在这种情况下，是一个自身形成凝聚态的场。它不需要电容器极板。它只需要能量达到特定状态，使得场自然发生偏移。这就是电子、夸克以及这些粒子的各种伴侣粒子——μ 粒子、τ

cues.en: lepton, all those ordinary and extraordinary particles, the fermions, get their mass by this phenomenon here. Phenomenon doesn't really have a name. It's called the spontaneous breaking of chiral symmetry, but it does have a name. But this is what it is. What about the zebozon? I told you before the zebozon is like a photon. Photons are massless. How does a zebozon get a mass?
cues.zh: 轻子，所有这些普通与非凡的粒子，即费米子，通过这里的这一现象获得质量的机制。这个现象其实没有特定的通俗名字。它被称为手征对称性自发破缺，其实它确实有个名字。但本质就是这样。那 Z 玻色子呢？我之前讲过 Z 玻色子就像光子。光子是没有质量的。Z 玻色子又是怎么获得质量的呢？

cues.en: So I'll just show you something very similar happens to the Z boson. Let's remind ourselves what a Z boson can do. It can take any particle which has a Zilch and in particular this green Ziggs particle. It can take the Ziggs particle and the Ziggs particle can emit a Z boson. It has charge, not real charge, but Zilch and Zilch emits Z bosons. All right, so now let's ask what that means.
cues.zh: 所以接下来我要给你们展示，类似的事情也发生在 Z 玻色子身上。我们先来回顾一下 Z 玻色子能做什么。它可以作用于任何带有 Zilch 荷的粒子，尤其是这个绿色的 Ziggs 粒子。它可以作用于 Ziggs 粒子，而 Ziggs 粒子可以发射一个 Z 玻色子。它带有电荷，不是真正的电荷，而是 Zilch，而带有 Zilch 的粒子会发射 Z 玻色子。好，现在我们来探究这意味着什么。

cues.en: That means that a Z boson moving along can do something a little bit similar to this. It can absorb some zilch out of the condensate, but now it has zilch. Originally it was just a Z boson. Z bosons don't have zilch. It absorbs some zilch and it becomes a ziggs. Z boson becomes a ziggs.
cues.zh: 这意味着，行进中的 Z 玻色子可以做出类似这样的举动。它可以从凝聚体中吸收一些 zilch，但现在它就拥有了 zilch。最初它只是个 Z 玻色子，Z 玻色子本身是没有 zilch 的。它吸收了一些 zilch，于是就变成了一个 ziggs。Z 玻色子变成了 ziggs。

cues.en: But then it can emit zigs, which gets lost in the condensate again. And the zebozon just moves on its merry way, constantly going back and forth from being a zebozon to being one of these imaginary, not imaginary, zig particles. That's the nature of the way that particles get mass from fields. This phenomenon
cues.zh: 但接着它又可以发射出 ziggs，重新消散在凝聚体中。而 Z 玻色子就这么优哉游哉地继续前行，不断地在 Z 玻色子和这种虚构的——也不能说是虚构的——zig 粒子之间来回切换。这就是粒子从场中获得质量的本质机制。这种现象，

cues.en: of the Z boson getting a mass is called the Braut-Angler-Higgs phenomenon. This is the one that's called the Higgs phenomenon, the Z boson getting a mass. Now this could have happened to the photon. Had there been a condensate of ordinary charged particles, the photon would have become massive. We would all be dead if that were the case. Massive photons would not be healthy for us.
cues.zh: 即 Z 玻色子获得质量的现象，被称为布劳特-恩格勒-希格斯机制（Brout-Englert-Higgs 机制）。这就是所谓的希格斯现象，即 Z 玻色子获得质量。其实光子原本也可能发生这种情况。如果存在普通带电粒子的凝聚体，光子就会拥有质量。要是那样的话，我们早就都没命了。有质量的光子对我们可没半点好处。

cues.en: And so we are very lucky that this phenomenon here did not apply to ordinary electric charge. Will we ever discover the Ziggs particle? Sure, we discovered it long ago. It's just part of the Z boson. The Z boson was discovered, I mean, it was postulated, though, in 1967, or even before that by many people.
cues.zh: 所以我们非常幸运，这种现象并没有发生在普通电荷上。那我们到底能不能发现 Ziggs 粒子呢？当然，我们很久以前就发现了。它其实就是 Z 玻色子的一部分。Z 玻色子被发现——我是说，虽然它在 1967 年，甚至更早以前就被很多人假定了存在。

cues.en: But it was discovered, I don't even remember what, around 1980? I forgot when the experiment of what SLAC first discovered the existence experimentally. But when it was discovered that there was a Z boson, that it had a mass, and that when its properties were studied, the properties were not only consistent, but required that it was a thing which went back and forth and back and forth and back and forth between pure Z boson and...
cues.zh: 但它被发现，我都记不清了，大概是在 1980 年左右？我忘了 SLAC 的实验最早是在什么时候通过实验证实它存在的了。但当人们发现存在 Z 玻色子、它拥有质量，并且研究了它的性质之后，发现这些性质不仅吻合，甚至必须要求它是一种在纯 Z 玻色子和……之间不断来回切换的东西。

cues.en: The ziggs particle so they've existed we're not in doubt about them, and we never were at least not for many years So far I have not mentioned the Higgs boson So what is the Higgs boson? Well the Higgs boson has to do with this condensate It has to do with this condensate But it's a different kind of excitation than sliding around the the edge of the sombrero here
cues.zh: 和 ziggs 粒子之间切换，所以它们是一直存在的，我们对其深信不疑，而且很多年来一直如此。到目前为止我还没提到过希格斯玻色子（Higgs boson）。那么希格斯玻色子究竟是什么呢？希格斯玻色子和这个凝聚体有关。它和这个凝聚体有关。但它不同于在这个墨西哥帽边缘来回滑动的那种激发。

cues.en: It does not have to move. It's not something which has to do with sliding around here. It has to do, I'll tell you two different ways to think about it. You have a condensate, and you can imagine the condensate has a density, a density of these fictitious particles in the condensate. Imagine something which changes the density of them, kind of like a sound wave, a compression wave of some kind.
cues.zh: 它不需要移动。它不是那种顺着帽檐滑动的东西。它有关的是——我可以给你们讲两种不同的理解方式。你有一团凝聚体，你可以想象凝聚体是有密度的，即凝聚体中这些虚构粒子的密度。想象一下有什么东西改变了它们的密度，有点像声波，某种压缩波。

cues.en: which squeezes them closer and further and closer apart, makes them more and more less dense. That kind of vibration is what a Higgs boson is. Another way to think about it is that it doesn't have to do with sliding around the periphery of the sombrero. It's go to a place in space and start the field oscillating this way. In and out this way.
cues.zh: 这让它们时而靠得更近，时而离得更远，密度也不断变疏变密。这种振动就是希格斯玻色子。另一种理解方式是，它并不是沿着墨西哥帽的边缘滑动，而是在空间的某个位置，让场开始这样振荡。像这样进进出出。

cues.en: The further away it is, the stronger the condensate. The closer to the center, the weaker the condensate. So when it sloshes back and forth, it's kind of a compressional wave in the condensate. That mode, that phenomenon, that oscillation is what is called a Higgs boson. The Higgs boson is like the sound wave propagating through the condensate.
cues.zh: 离中心越远，凝聚就越强；离中心越近，凝聚就越弱。所以当它来回晃动时，就类似于凝聚中的一种压缩波。那种模式、那种现象、那种振荡，就被称为希格斯玻色子。希格斯玻色子就像是在凝聚中传播的声波。

cues.en: The reason it has been so important is because it was the one element that had not yet been discovered. As I said, the Ziggs was discovered long ago. The Z and the W, the electrons, and all the others were discovered long ago. And so the next question, which I'll try to answer in a couple of, in five minutes, is why it was so hard to discover the Higgs, what we discovered about it, and
cues.zh: 它之所以如此重要，是因为它是唯一一个尚未被发现的元素。正如我所说，Ziggs 很久以前就被发现了，Z 玻色子、W 玻色子、电子以及其他所有粒子也早就被发现了。接下来我想用大概五分钟回答的问题是：为什么希格斯玻色子如此难以发现？我们发现了它的什么？以及……

cues.en: very, very quickly what the future might or might not bring. Try to do this in a couple of minutes. OK, so what kind of thing does the Higgs boson itself do? Now we're talking about the Higgs boson, not the Ziggs boson, not the Z-boson, the Higgs itself, the one that's been so elusive all these years. It's called H. And what it can do with some probability is, for example,
cues.zh: 非常简短地讲讲未来可能会带来什么，或者不会带来什么。我尽量在几分钟内讲完。好的，那么希格斯玻色子本身能做什么呢？现在我们讨论的是希格斯玻色子，不是 Ziggs 玻色子，也不是 Z 玻色子，而是希格斯粒子本身，就是这些年来一直难以捉摸的那个。它被称为 H。以一定的概率，它能做的事情比如……

cues.en: Create, we read this from left to right, the Higgs boson moving along in time, time is now to the left, can create an electron and a positron. It can create a pair of quarks. It can also create other things, a mu particle or a top quark or a bottom quark, all of the different quarks, electrons, also neutrinos, all of various fermions.
cues.zh: 产生……我们从左往右看，希格斯玻色子随时间推移——时间从左往右——可以产生一个电子和一个正电子。它可以产生一对夸克。它还可以产生其他粒子，比如μ子、顶夸克或底夸克，所有不同的夸克、电子，还有中微子，各种费米子……

cues.en: can be created in pairs when a Higgs boson decays. You say, if it's like a sound wave, why does it decay? Well, believe me, sound waves decay. If they didn't decay, you'd continue to hear my voice ring forever and ever, wouldn't you? So sound waves do decay. And it is possible to think of sound waves as decaying by creating particles. So the Higgs boson decays. It decays quickly if it exists, if it really exists. It decays quickly.
cues.zh: 都可以在希格斯玻色子衰变时成对产生。你可能会问，如果它像声波，那它为什么会衰变？相信我，声波也是会衰减的。如果不衰减，我的声音就会永远回荡下去，不是吗？所以声波确实会衰减。我们也可以把声波看作是通过产生粒子来进行衰变。因此希格斯玻色子会衰变。如果它存在，如果它真的存在，它衰变的速度非常快。它衰变极快。

cues.en: either into an electron positron or a pair of quarks, or maybe some other of the fermions that exist in nature. You can read this diagram in two different ways. Oh, incidentally, the probability that the Higgs decays like this is proportional to the mass of the particle that it decays into. The heavier the mass, the more strongly that particle is coupled to the Higgs boson.
cues.zh: 要么变成正负电子对，要么变成一对夸克，或者自然界中存在的其他费米子。你可以用两种不同的方式来理解这张图。顺便提一下，希格斯玻色子以这种方式衰变的概率，正比于它所衰变产物的粒子质量。质量越重，该粒子与希格斯玻色子的耦合就越强。

cues.en: So heavy particles are favored, and light particles are not favored. Now, you can read this diagram in either direction. You can say the Higgs boson decays, but you can also say an electron and a positron confuse together to make a Higgs boson. Well, if we want to make Higgs bosons and see them in the laboratory, we want to read the diagram from right to left. And we want to say this is a process.
cues.zh: 所以重粒子更受青睐，而轻粒子则不受青睐。现在，你可以从任意方向来理解这张图。你可以说希格斯玻色子发生了衰变，但你也可以说一个电子和一个正电子聚变在一起产生了希格斯玻色子。那么，如果我们想制造出希格斯玻色子并在实验室中观测到它们，我们就得从右往左看这张图。我们会说这是一个过程，

cues.en: whereby a pair of electrons can come together and make a Higgs boson. We've been colliding electrons and positrons for a long, long time. Almost as long as I've been a physicist, not quite. We've been colliding electrons and positrons together, and nobody was ever able to discover the Higgs. Now, one reason in the early days is it turns out that the Higgs is a fairly heavy particle. I will tell you what its mass is. But it's a fairly heavy particle, and unless you have enough energy,
cues.zh: 一对电子借此结合并产生一个希格斯玻色子。我们进行正负电子对撞已经有很长很长时间了。几乎和我当物理学家的时间一样长，虽然还差一点。我们一直在让电子和正电子碰撞，但从未有人能发现希格斯粒子。在早期，原因之一是希格斯粒子实际上是一个相当重的粒子。稍后我会告诉你们它的质量是多少。但它确实是个相当重的粒子，除非你有足够的能量，

cues.en: You don't have enough energy to make the Higgs boson, but there's a more important reason. In fact, Slack, in the later days of Slack's life, had plenty of energy to make the Higgs. The problem was the weakness of the coupling, the smallness of the mass of the electron translated into a very weak, improbable cross-section. Too small in effect, too unlikely to make the Higgs,
cues.zh: 否则就没有足够的能量来制造希格斯玻色子，但还有一个更重要的原因。事实上，SLAC 在其运行后期，已经拥有充足的能量来制造希格斯粒子了。问题出在耦合太弱，电子质量太小，导致截面非常微弱、概率极低。效应太微弱了，太不可能产生希格斯粒子了，

cues.en: And so when you collide electrons together at high energy, electrons are just not favorable. They're too light, and because they're light, they tend to not make Higgs with any appreciable probability. Well, how about quarks? We can collide quarks together. The usual quarks that make up the proton and neutron are also very light. And because they are light, also unlikely to ever make a Higgs boson. Well, I'm sure they were made in slack.
cues.zh: 因此，即使在高能下碰撞电子，电子也根本不合适。它们太轻了，正因为太轻，它们几乎不可能以任何可观的概率产生希格斯粒子。那夸克呢？我们可以把夸克撞在一起。构成质子和中子的常见夸克也非常轻。也正因为轻，同样极不可能产生希格斯玻色子。当然，我敢肯定 SLAC 当时确实产生过它们，

cues.en: but never in appreciable numbers that there was possible to detect them. So that was the main difficulty. The lightness of these particles was a thing that essentially prohibited us from making Higgs's in abundance at SLAC or in other laboratories where collisions took place. What is the most favorable particle, most likely particle, for the Higgs to decay in?
cues.zh: 但数量从未多到有可能探测出来的地步。所以这才是主要的困难所在。正是这些粒子的质量太轻，本质上阻碍了我们在 SLAC 或其他进行对撞的实验室中大量制造希格斯粒子。那么，希格斯粒子最倾向于、最可能衰变成什么粒子呢？

cues.en: the heaviest, the heaviest of the fermions, and the heaviest of the fermions is called the top quark. The top quark is hundreds and hundreds, thousands of times heavier than the electron, many thousands of times heavier than the electron, and the Higgs preferentially will decay into top quarks. So we'll just call those the quarks. They are quarks, but they're very heavy.
cues.zh: 最重的，最重的费米子，而最重的费米子被称为顶夸克。顶夸克的质量是电子的成百上千倍，甚至是几万倍，希格斯粒子会优先衰变成顶夸克。我们就暂且称它们为夸克吧。它们确实是夸克，但非常重。

cues.en: 170 times the mass of a proton, basically, which is heavy. Top and anti-top. Top quarks and anti-quarks. So you say, well, look, now it's easy to make the Higgs boson. You just, oh, actually, in fact, not possible for the Higgs to decay the two top quarks, because the two top quarks are too heavy. But if you read it the other way, and you take a pair of top quarks and collide them together, you can make a Higgs.
cues.zh: 质量基本上是质子的 170 倍，这非常重了。顶夸克和反顶夸克。顶夸克和反夸克。所以你可能会说，看吧，现在制造希格斯玻色子很容易了。你只要……噢，实际上，希格斯粒子不可能衰变成两个顶夸克，因为两个顶夸克太重了。但如果你反过来理解，拿一对顶夸克并将它们撞在一起，你就能制造出希格斯粒子。

cues.en: So it's easy. We just go in the laboratory, take a pair of top quarks, collide them together, and make a Higgs. Well, the problem is that it's not so easy to find top quarks in nature. Why not? They decay very rapidly to the other quarks. They're not sitting around. You can't put them into the accelerator and accelerate them. They disappear in a tiny fraction of a second. There are no top quarks sitting around.
cues.zh: 所以这很简单。我们直接去实验室，找一对顶夸克，让它们对撞，就能造出希格斯粒子。但问题是，在自然界中并不容易找到顶夸克。为什么呢？它们会极其迅速地衰变成其他夸克。它们不会老老实实待在那儿。你没法把它们放进加速器里去加速。它们在一瞬间就消失了。周围根本就没有现成的顶夸克。

cues.en: Not even buried inside protons and so forth. Not even buried inside other kinds of particles. There are no top quarks around. So we have to make the top quarks somehow in the collision. How do you make a top quark? Alright, so here's a way to make a top quark. A gluon can come along. This is a gluon now. And remember what gluons do. They couple to quarks. One possibility is that the gluon
cues.zh: 甚至连质子等粒子内部也没有。其他任何种类的粒子内部都没有。周围根本不存在顶夸克。所以我们必须在碰撞中以某种方式造出顶夸克。那怎么造顶夸克呢？好，这里有一种造顶夸克的方法。可以来一个胶子。现在这是一个胶子。记住胶子的作用，它们会与夸克耦合。一种可能性是，这个胶子

cues.en: can make a top quark and an anti-top quark. Well, there's plenty of gluons around, as we'll see in a moment. So why don't we just take a gluon and make a top quark and an anti-top quark out of it. The reason is because gluons are very light. They're almost massless. They don't weigh very much. Top quarks are very heavy. There's simply not enough energy in the gluon to create a pair of top quarks.
cues.zh: 能产生一个顶夸克和一个反顶夸克。等会儿我们就会看到，周围其实到处都是胶子。那为什么我们不直接用一个胶子，让它产生一个顶夸克和一个反顶夸克呢？原因在于胶子非常轻。它们几乎没有质量，没什么重量。而顶夸克非常重。单个胶子根本没有足够的能量来创造一对顶夸克。

cues.en: So what we have to do is we have to take a pair of gluons, now here's a process that you can imagine, take a pair of gluons with a lot of energy moving toward each other with a huge speed, plenty of energy, let one of them make a pair of top quarks for a short period of time and then let the other one come and be absorbed by one of the top quarks. There we have it, a pair of top quarks.
cues.zh: 所以我们必须用一对胶子，你可以想象这样一个过程：用一对拥有巨大能量的胶子，以极高的速度相向运动，能量充沛，让其中一个在短时间内产生一对顶夸克，然后让另一个过来被其中一个顶夸克吸收。这样一来，我们就得到了一对顶夸克。

cues.en: created by a pair of gluons, a pair of high-energy gluons smashed together and make a pair of top quarks.
